You will review the rule against speeding in a work zone, where a work zone begins and ends, how an added penalty works, what orange signs and Flagger signs mean, why the handbook says to act early on advance signs, the risk of driving slower than the traffic around you, and the devices used to guide drivers. A highway work zone runs from the first sign marking where the zone begins to the last sign marking where it ends. If a sign at the start of a work zone lists a speeding penalty, that penalty is added on top of any other penalty for the speeding conviction. So the posted limit applies for the whole stretch between the first and last work zone signs. The zone boundaries come from the signs, and so does the extra penalty. If the starting sign lists a penalty, it is added to the regular speeding penalty. So when you see orange signs, you know you are approaching or inside a work zone, and the rules from the previous slides apply. So the handbook asks for two things together in work zones. Respond to advance signs early, moving over when they tell you to. So in a work zone, follow the path these devices lay out, watch for the signs that tell you to change lanes early, and keep to the posted limit from the first work zone sign to the last.
